assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: Acute hematogenous osteomyelitis is the most common manifestation of osteomyelitis in children and evolves secondary to bacteremia

assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: Subacute osteomyelitis usually follows local inoculation by penetrating trauma

assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: Subacute osteomyelitis usually follows local inoculation by penetrating trauma and is not associated with systemic symptoms

assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: In children beyond the newborn period and without hemoglobinopathies, bone infections occur almost exclusively in the metaphysis of long bones

assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: Preceding nonpenetrating trauma is often reported and may lead to local bone injury that predisposes to infection

assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: Bone infections in children with sickle cell disease occur in the diaphyseal portion of the long bones

assertions.subject: Osteomyelitis
assertions.quote: In children younger than 12 to 18 months of age, capillaries perforate the epiphyseal growth plate, permitting spread of infection across the epiphysis leading to suppurative arthritis
